speaker: Ben Bloom, CEO, Atom Computing

checkins.note: A January 2025 report describes an on-premise system from the same Atom Computing/Microsoft partnership supporting up to 50 logical qubits -- more than this claim's own 24, which is why this is logged on_track rather than off_track. Not treated as a resolution: the desk still needs to confirm this is the SAME delivery the original claim described, not a different, larger, later system being counted as satisfying an earlier, smaller promise.

sourcing_note: Deadline (31 Dec 2025 + 30-day grace = 30 Jan 2026) has passed as of capture (2026-08-27). Flagged resolvable by the seeding pass, NOT resolved -- a January 2025 follow-up report (HPCwire) described Atom Computing and Microsoft rolling out an on-premise system supporting up to 50 logical qubits, which reads as meeting or exceeding this claim, but the desk should verify the exact 24-logical-qubit specification was what actually shipped before writing a VERIFIED verdict, per the two-key rule.
verbatim: By coupling our state-of-the-art neutral-atom qubits with Microsoft's qubit-virtualization system, we are now able to offer reliable logical qubits on a commercial quantum machine.
headline: Atom Computing and Microsoft announced a commercial quantum machine with 24 entangled logical qubits, available for delivery in 2025.
resolution_criteria: Resolves VERIFIED if a commercial customer actually received and operated a system matching the 24-entangled-logical-qubit specification by 31 Dec 2025 (plus grace) -- an order or a demo does not count, an operating delivered system does. PARTIALLY_VERIFIED if a related but differently-specified system shipped in the window (e.g. a different logical-qubit count) instead of the exact one announced. NOT_VERIFIED if no delivery happened in the stated window at all.
